correctness.rationale: Leaf-pair elimination gives rank 2ν on forests with nonzero edge weights, over any field. For an attached tree T with bridge endpoint u, restriction to the coordinate hyperplane u=0 has the same rank exactly when some radical vector has nonzero u-coordinate; otherwise that hyperplane maps to a hyperplane of the symplectic quotient and the rank drops by two. This is the frozen matching-essentiality test. Split the tree form into a nondegenerate complement and its radical. Eliminating the nondegenerate block does not change other entries: the bridge meets only one cycle vertex and the self-pairing is zero. A nonessential root leaves a radical vector paired with that cycle vertex v. Eliminating this pair leaves the unchanged forest on the remaining vertices (and zero radical coordinates). The matching number in this case is ν(T)+1+ν(H−(T∪{v})), using the bridge plus maxima in T−u and the remaining forest, and at most one matching edge incident to v. If every root is essential, the cycle survives unchanged and maximum matching sizes add. The odd cycle has maximal possible rank by deleting one vertex; the even cycle loses exactly two ranks on equality of its alternating products (a vertex-deleted path gives the lower bound). Solving for one nonzero cycle weight gives precisely (q−1)^(|S|−1) exceptional assignments. For odd q the class-two coadjoint orbit for a fixed edge functional of rank 2r has size q^(2r) and degree q^r, giving q^(n−2r) characters per such functional. A bounded independent GF(4) enumeration of a square, square with a leaf and square with a two-edge tail gave, in increasing half-rank, (1,75,180), (1,123,900), and (1,135,1800,2160). On full support the exceptional counts were 27, 0 and 243, respectively, as predicted.
residual_risks: The numerical check is only a corroboration over an extension field; the matching and alternating-form arguments establish the general rank formula. No characteristic-two character claim is assessed.

evidence: Li–Yu uses exactly the saturation test in structural rank results for unweighted oriented graphs, not all nonzero finite-field weights. Hou–Lei's evenly linear subgraph expansion exposes the matching/cycle terms for unweighted orientations.
Rossmann links the graphical-group degree enumerator to support-constrained alternating matrix ranks. The exact indexed factorization covers arbitrary attached trees and all prime powers for ranks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The fixed-orientation and general group frameworks account for tools in the proof, but do not give the distribution by themselves. In contrast the distinct exact factorization is already a formula for the full distribution. No claim about the scope of the inaccessible Gong–Xu formula is necessary to the decision.

evidence: The two distinct exact records give equivalent conditions on each support, the same rank decrement, and the same q domains for rank and character statements. The root-deletion equality in Q_v is equivalent to forbidding a matching gain through any bridge at v.
Rossmann's general bridge explains why identical rank polynomials give identical degree counts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The frozen result is directly implied by either of these extant explicit formulations without new field hypotheses or a new enumeration. This establishes non-distinctness, not historical priority relative to the frozen record.

evidence: The first record has the identical two support sums and character coefficient formula with correction indicator δ(F)=1 iff the full cycle is even and all maximum matchings pair its vertices using cycle edges.
The second gives the same dependence on even complete support and cycle-product cancellation, with product of Q_v factors testing ν_v(S)=ν_v^0(S).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: On a support with full cycle of length 2m, put M_0=m+Σ_Tν(T). If all bridge roots are essential, using any bridge costs one in that tree's internal matching, and at least one cycle edge is lost from the perfect cycle matching; hence all maxima perfectly match the cycle internally. If some root u is nonessential, use its bridge, maxima off-cycle leaving u free, and an (m−1)-matching on the cycle minus its bridge vertex, getting a size-M_0 matching using a bridge. This is either maximum or a greater maximum must also use a bridge, proving equivalence to δ. In the supported rooted tree at v, ν_v(S) exceeds ν_v^0(S) precisely if some bridge from v meets a nonessential branch root. Thus the Q_v factors select exactly the same exceptional supports; on such supports ν(S)=M_0, giving the identical factorized sum.

originality.rationale: Distinct indexed records contain the same full all-field rank enumerator, supportwise rank-drop condition, and odd-field character enumerator. The first uses the equivalent condition that every maximum support matching pairs the entire cycle internally; the second gives an equivalent factorization over rooted trees. This is verified existing coverage of the mathematical claim, not a finding about priority or who discovered it first. The path dates differ, but do not independently establish priority or lineage. The frozen proof is correct, yet no distinct surviving theorem is established by the different presentation.
residual_risks: Priority and the relationship among the distinct record histories have not been established by these source comparisons.
Gong–Xu full text was not retrieved; it might add antecedents. That limitation is not the basis of the failure.

value.rationale: As mathematics the full enumerator is useful: it classifies all assignments, distinguishes a leaf from an even-length tail via a precise combinatorial test, and converts the result into degree multiplicities in a natural family of graphical groups. This is a general structural formula rather than an arbitrary small example. That usefulness does not make this presentation a distinct contribution given the verified coverage.
residual_risks: The sum can be exponential in the edge count and does not extend by this proof to graphs with multiple cycles.
